title: [C18T2] - Number of US households by annual income
prompt: The graph below shows the number of households in the US by their annual income in 2007, 2011 and 2015. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of American households across five income brackets over three specific years 2007, 2011 and 2015.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the figures remained relatively stable for most income groups throughout the period shown, with the notable exception of households earning $100,000 or more, which saw a significant increase. Additionally, the two most common income brackets were consistently $25,000-$49,999 and $100,000 or more.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the growing categories, in 2007, the $100,000+ group led with 29 million households, followed by the $25,000-$49,999 and under $25,000 bracket, with the respective figures of 27 million and 25 million. Subsequently, the highest income group showed the most substantial growth, rising to 33 million by 2015, making it the largest category. By 2015, both lower income groups first increased significantly in 2011 before declining, with households earning under $25,000 and $25,000-$49,999 falling to 27 and 28 million, respectively, though both still showed overall growth from their 2007 levels.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the stable income groups, in 2007, around 21 million households earned between $50,000 and $74,999, which was 7 million higher than the $75,000-$99,999 bracket. While the former group maintained exactly the same numbers throughout the period, the latter showed minimal variation, declining slightly to 13 million in 2011 before rising to 15 million by 2015.
